items.title: Pillow CVE-2026-112900: How to find and fix it with GitLab
items.summary: GitLab is not affected by CVE-2026-112900 or the other vulnerabilities fixed in Pillow 13.0.0. GitLab products do not include the Pillow library, and our Security team has found no evidence of impact to GitLab-managed infrastructure. GitLab.com, GitLab Self-Managed, and GitLab Dedicated are not impacted.Pillow is one of the most widely used image libraries in the Python ecosystem. It often sits several layers down in a dependency tree, pulled in by a web framework, a thumbnailing service or an ML toolkit that nobody chose it for directly. On October 16, 2026, the Pillow project released version 13.0.0, and one of its security fixes is CVE-2026-112900: an argument injection in the way Pillow calls Ghostscript to render EPS images. The CVE record, published on October 19, rates it 9.2 (Critical) on CVSS 4.0. It affects every Pillow release from 2.6.0 up to, but not including, 13.0.0. No exploitation in the wild has been reported so far, but CISA's assessment marks it as automatable with total technical impact.Upgrade Pillow to 13.0.0 on every project and image that handles untrusted images, and remove Ghostscript from images that do not need EPS support.This guide is for security and platform teams with Python projects on GitLab. It covers the fixed version for each distribution, how the flaw works, the other High and Critical issues fixed in the same release, how to locate affected projects with dependency scanning, container scanning, GitLab Orbit, and code search, and how to remediate at scale with GitLab Duo Agent Platform.CVE-2026-112900 at a glanceCVE-2026-112900 is an OS command and argument injection flaw in Pillow's EPS plugin, rated Critical (CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2) by the CVE Numbering Authority (CNA). The CVE record was published on October 19, 2026.FieldDetailCVECVE-2026-112900GitHub advisoryGHSA-w889-685w-c8fhTitlePillow: Argument Injection in Ghostscript call, potentially leading into RCEWeaknessCWE-88 (argument injection), CWE-78 (OS command injection)CVSS 4.09.2 Critical (AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H)Affected versionsPillow >= 2.6.0 and < 13.0.0Fixed inPillow 13.0.0Exploitation statusNone known at the time of writing (CISA SSVC assessment dated October 20, 2026)Upgrade Pillow to a fixed version nowUpgrade Pillow to 13.0.0 or later. The CVE record lists 13.0.0 as the only fixed version, so every older branch needs to move to it. Framework updates and input validation on image contents do not help here, because the flaw is in how the filename reaches Ghostscript.Your Python versionWhat to do3.11 to 3.15Upgrade with pip install --upgrade "pillow>=13.0.0", or raise the pin in your lockfile or requirements file.If your Pillow comes from a distribution package, check the distribution's tracker first. Distribution packages keep their own version numbers, so compare against the tracker instead of pip show. Status as of October 26, 2026:DistributionPillow package versionStatusDebian 12 (bookworm)9.4.0-1.1+deb12u1Vulnerable, no fix yetDebian 13 (trixie)11.1.0-5+deb13u4Vulnerable, no fix yetDebian forky (testing)12.3.0-1Vulnerable, no fix yetDebian sid (unstable)13.0.0-1FixedSUSE Linux Enterprise (Server 15 SP4 to SP7 and 16.0 to 16.2, among others) and openSUSE Leap 16.0 and 16.1python-PillowAffected, no fix listedAmazon Linux 2023 and 2027 Previewpython-pillowPending fixSources: Debian, SUSE and Amazon Linux security trackers, as of October 26, 2026. Amazon Linux 2 is listed as not affected. Ubuntu lists all releases as needing evaluation, and Red Hat, Arch Linux and Oracle Linux had no record for this CVE. Alpine's tracker could not be checked.Until your distribution ships a fix, install Pillow 13.0.0 from PyPI in a virtual environment or container, or apply the workarounds below.Rebuild your container images. If your Dockerfile installs Pillow without pinning a patch version, rebuild it with docker build --pull --no-cache and redeploy it so the install step resolves the fixed release. Images that pin a version, such as pillow==12.3.0, need the pin changed first. Images built on top of other base images only get the fix once their maintainers update them, so check the upstream image before you rebuild.Pillow 13.0.0 also changes a few behaviors, such as how duplicate TIFF tags are handled and how I-mode images are saved as PNG, so run your image-processing tests before you ship the upgrade.How the vulnerability worksEPS files are PostScript programs, so Pillow shells out to Ghostscript (gs) to render them, passing the input filename right after -f with no sanitizing.When the image object has a .name that exists on disk, Pillow used that name as-is. Ghostscript's argument parser gives two kinds of strings special meaning:A leading - is read as an option rather than a filename, which gives an attacker argument injection (CWE-88).A leading @ tells Ghostscript to read more command-line arguments from the named text file.
